  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Assembly
Bill 361, please note that members of the public will only be allowed
to observe and address the Planning Commission of January 18,2022 at
7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other means, as follows:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 6883764#

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:
   When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
   If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an area
  with good reception.
   If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the
  sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from the
  phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to feedback.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to Mindy
Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Planning Commission prior
to consideration of the agenda, comments must be received prior to
12:00 P.M. on January 18, 2022 the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 12:00 P.M. and prior to close of the public hearing will be
made part of the official public record of the meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California
90301.  All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours
prior to the day of the hearing.

5B. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) CHAPTER 12 IMC:
A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001
(ZCA-2020-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to
modify regulations for off-hour parking for major event patrons and
tailgating, citywide.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick stated that she had no questions.

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

Commissioner Rice stated to staff:
 This model does not work. True that the Arenas and Stadiums may
  need local parking for several of their events that will take place
  here in this city, and you are speaking of tying-up a minimum of
  6 to 8 hours of parking spaces which will include coming early to
  get the parking space, staying late to retrieve the parked vehicle,
  and a minimum charge of at least $25.00 per car at maybe a total
  of 10 parking spaces several of the community businesses will
  attempt to assist the arena/stadium meaning a possible $250.00 an
  event, but this business model does not work, just on the parking
  alone.

Commissioner Patrick stated she did have a question for staff:
 Tailgating parking usually occurs on Sundays, and to be located
  in the areas of the stadium seems alright, but in the Marketplace
  which is generally utilized by the public for shopping on those
  days, will there be a designated location set-aside for the
  tailgating/parking of those vehicles during game day where the
  public will not be put out of their parking space convenience?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated they would have to obtain a Special Use Permit,
  because the businesses would be open and operating at the same
  time, therefore they would have to demonstrate that they have
  the additional parking spaces available.

Chairman Springs asked Ms. Wilcox;
 For clarification that the businesses would have to obtain a
  Special Use Permit prior to hosting any form of Tailgating and that
  the proper amount of spaces must be available for them to utilize
  their place of business?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that in order for businesses to do tailgating,
  they would have to be in the C-R Zone near the stadium and Forum,
  along with have the additional parking spaces that would be
  designated for the use of tailgating while they are conducting
  regular business. They would be required to obtain Permits and
  Licensing approval and either demonstrate excess Parking
  Available Or provide a Parking Study and request a Special Use
  Permit to allow for the shared overlapping parking usage.

Commissioner Rice asked Ms. Wilcox;
 Please show the C-R Zone that would allow the tailgating parking.
 In getting an understanding, are the Forum and Stadium attempting
  to create a partnership with the community in order to lighten the
  parking load and impact on the stadium and forum is this correct?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the new stadium along with the forum have
  a substantial amount of parking already built-in and available
  for their use.
 If we were to take all of the main arteries into the stadium
  location – La Brea, Prairie, Crenshaw, Florence, Century
  Boulevards, all of those streets that could lighten the impact of
  vehicle parking that would be in the entertainment district, but
  why would the City with no incentives for the property owners, why
  not allow them tailgating to potentially engage with the people
  who would be utilizing their property, especially since they are
  small lots. For a four to six hour holding location for these
  vehicles to come early and do what, since they cannot tailgate,
  to just sit for four to six hours prior to a game looking and
  watching people go by? What would make the property owners want
  to come to City Hall to obtain the permits needed? They could claim
  these people as guest and friends, come and park for four hours,
  and therefore not need to obtain the permits for tailgating. Most
  likely their lot or area would only hold close to 10 to 12
  additional vehicles.
